```

pytest honors CLI order, so naming the two tests in reversed order is enough to trigger it. Running the whole file in reverse definition order fails 4 of 22 tests (`test_async_state`, `test_sync_state`, `test_async_raise_other`, `test_sync_raise_other`), and random shuffles (for example under pytest-randomly) fail 2 to 4 tests depending on the seed.

This PR resets the shared state between tests with an autouse fixture, the same pattern `tests/test_dependency_yield_except_httpexception.py` already uses for the same reason. The file now passes in definition order, reversed, and shuffled. The reset cannot change what the existing tests check: every `errors` assertion is a membership check after the test's own request, and every `state` assertion reads keys the test itself transitions.

Tests only, no library changes.
